To: d.kerrigan@northmail.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr Kerrigan,

Thank you for contacting Erindale Park Pharmacy. We would be pleased to help your mother with her medications as she returns home. I understand you would like everything arranged before Thursday, and I want to make sure you have a clear plan for the first few days.

We prepare weekly blister packs covering seven days, with up to four medication times each day. There is no charge for the packaging itself. The usual prescription charges still apply; Ontario Drug Benefit covers most eligible prescription costs for seniors, although any applicable deductible or co-payment remains payable.

We can deliver to your mother’s building. Our regular delivery service is free within eight kilometres, on Tuesdays and Fridays between 2 and 6 p.m. You are also welcome to collect her packs. For her first packs, we can arrange a one-time Saturday delivery before 1 p.m. if that would be more convenient.

To transfer her prescriptions, please provide her current pharmacy’s name and address and call us with her OHIP number rather than sending it by email. We will contact the pharmacy to arrange the transfer; no transfer form is required.

Please ask the hospital discharge team to fax her discharge prescriptions to us early Thursday. Preparing the first packs takes approximately 48 hours after we receive all prescriptions, including the transfers, so Saturday is our expected start, provided everything arrives in time. We will confirm when they are ready.

Her first blister packs will not be ready when she leaves hospital. Before discharge, please confirm with the discharge team that she will have an interim medication supply and that someone will help her with every dose until Saturday’s pickup or delivery. This is particularly important with several new medications.

I would be happy to review her medication list with you once we have your mother’s permission. We record this using our Family Communication Consent form, signed by Margaret. This protects her privacy while allowing us to involve you in her care as she wishes. She can sign at pickup, or we can send the form with the delivery driver. We can still coordinate general arrangements with you beforehand.

I would also like to offer a MedsCheck at her home during her first week back, to review her medications and answer questions. It takes about 20 minutes. I can visit Monday or Tuesday after 6 p.m.; please let me know which evening would suit her.

My direct line is 905-555-0148 ext. 2. I am in the store Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Please let me know a suitable evening time to speak, your preferred Saturday collection or delivery option, and whether the interim arrangements have been confirmed.

Kind regards,
Rania Haddad
Community Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
